Maria R: Quick question — as we start nudging customers to v2, what will routing do for v1 tokens by default? throttled? auto-mapped? need to update console copy and the migration checklist :thinking:

Jon P: Default plan was soft-redirect: if token explicitly requests v1 via `X-Redwood-Version: 1` keep them on v1. Otherwise use token->route affinity to pick v2 where possible, fall back to v1 when capacity spikes. that still accurate?

Sasha: That's the current runtime behavior, yes. Two gotchas: 1) tenants with reserved capacity pinned to v1 will always stay on v1. 2) we auto-map unauthenticated routes to v2 for cost reasons, which surprises some folks.

Maria R: Right — product wants a single-liner in the console: "Requests without explicit version header will route to the latest compatible runtime (may be v2)." Is that technically true?

Sasha: Mostly. We should add a clause about deterministic affinity so users know routing isn't random. proposed: "If no version is specified, routing chooses the default runtime based on tenant settings and capacity; pinned tenants remain on their pinned version."

Lin: We need to be careful with quota/telemetry too. If we silently route v1 tokens to v2, we distort per-version telemetry and cost allocation. Suggest emitting a derived metric `routing.effective_version` with values [v1,v2] per request + header about `X-Routing-Decision: mapped-to-v2` for debuggability.

Jon P: Agree on metric. Also recommend we tag the token-level billing record with `served_version` so billing/chargeback matches. That will require a small change in usage pipeline (kafka event field).

Sasha: Implementation detail: runtime can add header `X-Runtime-Served-Version: v2` before response. ops can strip it for public API, but console and debug logs keep it. Deploy plan: add header in runtime -> ship to staging -> add metric in ingestion pipeline.

deploy-bot: deploy-prod v2-runtime-service started by @Sasha — build 2026.03.18-rc3

Maria R: UX question — when we show a tenant's "migration readiness" card in console, should we warn if we see >10% of recent requests auto-mapped from v1->v2? product wants a polite nudge: "We mapped some requests to v2 to save cost; pin to v1 if you need strict behavior."

Lin: +1 for the nudge. Also surface a small traffic timeline that colors mapped requests separately. Two signals to include: `mapped_pct_last_1h` and `errors_after_map`. If errors spike after mapping, we should auto-open an alert to SRE.

Jon P: For rollouts, add a runtime flag `--mapping-threshold=0.2` that disables mapping if >20% of a tenant's request rate would be remapped (avoids large surprise changes). we can make it configurable per-tenant via console toggle.

Sasha: I'll draft the runtime PR. Lin, can you prototype the metric and a sample event schema? Maria, I'll sync on the console copy after PR lands.

Lin: I'll drop an example kafka payload in #eng-infra later today. sample field: \"served_version\":\"v2\", \"mapping_reason\":\"capacity-savings\"

Maria R: Awesome. Action items: Sasha PR for header+flag, Lin schema + ingestion spike check, Jon add billing tag and console toggle wiring, Maria will update console copy + migration hint. Thanks :thumbsup:

Jon P: One more: we should document the fallback semantics in the API docs under "Versioning and routing" with a tiny example: ```http
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <token>
# no X-Redwood-Version header -> routing decided by tenant affinity/capacity
```

Sasha: noted. tagging @product for FYI.

Maria R: closing loop — will follow up with final console strings once I see the PR.
